ip_top_stories.title: Sony Copyright Suit Survives AI Music Generator's Dismissal Bid
ip_top_stories.summary: A court has allowed Sony's copyright infringement lawsuit against an AI music generator to proceed, rejecting the defendant's attempt to have the case dismissed. The ruling is a significant development in ongoing litigation over AI-generated music and the use of copyrighted material in training or output. The case is being closely watched as a bellwether for AI music copyright disputes.

ip_top_stories.title: Copyright owners v AI developers: the emerging trends
ip_top_stories.summary: An analysis of the developing legal landscape between copyright holders and AI developers, mapping emerging trends in how courts and legislators are approaching these disputes. The piece examines patterns across multiple jurisdictions as cases and regulatory frameworks continue to evolve.

ip_top_stories.title: Monkey selfie from 15 years ago accidentally sets precedent for AI copyright dispute
ip_top_stories.summary: The landmark 'monkey selfie' case, which established that non-human entities cannot hold copyright, is now being cited as relevant precedent in AI copyright disputes over who — if anyone — owns AI-generated works. Legal commentators are examining how the ruling's logic applies to content produced by artificial intelligence systems.

ip_top_stories.title: EU copyright law roundup – first trimester of 2026
ip_top_stories.summary: IPKat's quarterly roundup covers key EU copyright law developments in the first three months of 2026, including legislative updates and case law relevant to AI and digital content. The roundup provides a structured overview of how EU frameworks are adapting to emerging AI and intellectual property challenges.

ip_top_stories.title: AI Makes Securing Copyright Protection for Software Code Tricky Guide
ip_top_stories.summary: A legal guide examines the complications arising when AI is used to generate or assist in writing software code, particularly around securing copyright protection for the resulting work. The piece outlines the key ambiguities under current law and practical considerations for developers and companies.

ip_further_links.title: Is the government's stance on AI copyright holding back the UK tech scene?
ip_further_links.summary: An examination of whether the UK government's current approach to AI copyright exceptions is hampering domestic technology development, with perspectives from industry and legal commentators.

ip_further_links.title: AI Startups Have These Copyright Lawyers on Speed Dial
ip_further_links.summary: A look at the specialist copyright lawyers increasingly retained by AI startups to navigate training data disputes, licensing negotiations, and litigation exposure.

ip_further_links.title: Who owns AI copyright when machines create art?
ip_further_links.summary: An overview of the unresolved legal question of ownership over AI-generated creative works, surveying current positions across different jurisdictions.

ip_further_links.title: Analysing China's stricter examination standards for AI-related patent applications
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of China's tightened patent examination criteria for AI-related inventions and what the changes mean for applicants.

ip_further_links.title: AI-generated content should be clearly labelled to help people spot fakes, committee says
ip_further_links.summary: A parliamentary or legislative committee has recommended mandatory labelling of AI-generated content to help the public identify synthetic media, according to The Globe and Mail.

ip_further_links.title: Anthropic Code Crisis Creates Copyright Contradiction
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of copyright tensions arising from Anthropic's AI coding tools, examining contradictions between the company's public positions and its use of potentially copyrighted code.

ip_further_links.title: AI in the patent industry: Don't believe the hype. Believe the data.
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat examines empirical data on AI adoption in the patent industry, arguing that actual usage patterns diverge significantly from the hype surrounding AI-powered patent tools.

ip_further_links.title: Bologna Children's Book Fair 2026: AI Takes Center Stage
ip_further_links.summary: Publishers Weekly reports that AI was a dominant theme at the 2026 Bologna Children's Book Fair, with discussions centred on AI-generated illustration, authorship, and the implications for publishing rights.

ip_further_links.title: Guest Post — Exploring Data Spaces in Scholarly Communications
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen explores the concept of data spaces in scholarly communications, examining how shared data infrastructure could affect rights management and licensing for academic content.

ip_further_links.title: GitHub Policy Update
ip_further_links.summary: GitHub has updated its policies in ways relevant to AI-generated code, copyright, and developer rights, with implications for how AI coding tools interact with open-source licensing.
